newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares lose 0.65 pct, awaiting political news.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares lose 0.65 pct, awaiting political news.

text.p: Istanbul shares dropped amid sharply lower volume on Wednesday as political concerns continued to weigh on prices, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,673, down 11 points, or 0.65 percent from Tuesday. It had dived 5.07 percent on Tuesday after soaring 8.04 percent on Monday on political developments.
Trade volume was almost halved to 18.64 trillion lira ($127.1 million) from Tuesday's 34.42 trillion ($235 million).
The market worries that a new coalition planned by Prime Minister-Designate Mesut Yilmaz to exclude the Islamist Welfare, the biggest party in parliament, may not win a confidence vote.
"The market will probably enliven when Yilmaz presents a cabinet list to the President but will again settle down afterwards to wait for the confidence vote," smail Gner from Info Securities said.
"If Yilmaz gets the vote, then the bourse is likely to exceed its trading record of 1,780," he added.

President Suleyman Demirel appointed conservative opposition leader Yilmaz last week to form a coalition to replace the one-year-old government under Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who resigned last week under army pressure.
Yilmaz has said he would present Demirel with a cabinet list on June 30.

He has won the backing of two left-wing parties, a secularist small right-wing grouping and conservative independents, but needs the support of around a dozen MPs from rival conservative True Path Party (DYP) to win the vote.
DYP leader Tansu Ciller who allied with Erbakan, has rejected an offer from Yilmaz to join his planned alliance.
